differences.what: massing: the draft's 13 m hipped box is now the photograph's house: two tall storeys over a high basement under a slated mansard with a crested deck, the library pavilion at the south end carried up into a steep gable with a finial, the porch and balcony before the hall, and the steep slated pyramid over the north-east corner; the pavilion's finial prints at y 115 px against the photograph's 290 (the gable steeper and about 2 m taller than the photograph's), the pyramid's at y 45 against 100
the front's width: the body is widened to the 1911 outline's 14.2 m, and the pavilion's south edge, the porch and the corner now print within about 30-60 px of the photograph together
heights: the balcony's floor and the cornice's foot print within about 20 px of the photograph's (y 893 and 640 px)

the corner (T-3700): the photograph's oriel at the second storey over the cut corner now stands there, a turned stone square on its corbel courses at the second floor, its face to the corner about 2.2 m across with its pair of lights (y 690-860 px; the render's within about 20 px) and a narrow light on each cheek, on the 1876 plate's stone column with its capital (the photograph's tree hides the column); the record's square brick tower from grade is gone. The parlour's corner behind the column stands square where the plan cuts it, which the tree hides here

the corner's pyramid (T-3700): it now springs from the oriel's eaves on the main cornice's line, behind the oriel's gable, flared at its foot and steep above, its tip at about y 130-150 px against the photograph's 130; the photograph's stands a little wider at its foot than the oriel's cornice

the oriel's gable (T-3700): the photograph's and the plate's small coped stone gable over the oriel's face, a roundel in its tympanum (y 560-655 px), now stands on the oriel's eaves before the pyramid; the plate's carved rose in the roundel is a plain disc

the library pavilion's gable panel (T-3702): the photograph's pale carved field in the gable's apex now stands there, K08's dressed gable panel under the copings with its carved relief; the photograph's carving is a diaper lattice and the panel's is K08's leaf relief, and the panel fills the whole gable over the pavilion's top light where the photograph's stops at a stone band over the gable's light

the library pavilion's gable: the photograph's rakes flare out at their feet over slated cheeks, with kneeler blocks; the record's coping runs straight to its kneelers (K08's coped gable does not flare), and the pavilion stands 0.8 m out where the plan draws about 1.25

the porch (T-3701): it now stands on the photograph's axis, 0.5 m north of the door, its slab and columns within about 40 px of the photograph's (they printed about 80 px south), the soffit lowered so the deep entablature prints with the photograph's (the capitals at about y 1075 px), the guard raised to the photograph's 0.85 m (its top within about 10 px of y 890) before a door onto the balcony, and the capitals carved

the porch's cluster and reach: the photograph's balcony runs on south to the pavilion on stone piers, and its north corner is a cluster of three slender columns on a pedestal about 1.4 m high; the record's porch is 3.2 m wide on one column a side on 0.8 m pedestals (K01's porch columns stand at least 0.3 m apart past their plinths, and its porch stands only on its own landing); the balustrade's carved pierced panels are square stone balusters

the stoop (T-3701): the flight now rises between swept stone cheeks, splayed toward the walk as the plate's plan draws it, the south cheek pierced by a row of openings under its coping as the photograph's is; the photograph's flight is about 2.3 m between its cheeks and north of the porch's middle where the record's is the porch's 3.2 m, its cheeks' heads stand about 0.2 m higher than the kit's highest, and its north cheek's carved roundel is not built; the 'second flight from the south' is in neither picture (the photograph's left-hand flight is this flight's south cheek), so nothing is built for it

the stone bands (T-3699): the photograph's pale stone against the dark brick in three bands — the stone carried on over the principal floor to the principal lights' sills, a deep band from the principal heads to the second-storey sills (the arches and the balcony's string course in it), and the frieze under the cornice — are now laid on the front's parlour bay and along the 21st Street flank at the record's own sill and head lines; at the parlour the deep band prints at y 950-1050 px against the photograph's 905-1060. The flank's deep band prints taller than the photograph's because the record's flank lights are shorter than the photograph's (the flank's lights are their own difference, below); the south flank is carried round the same way

the library pavilion's bands and base: the photograph carries the same pale bands and the stone basement across the pavilion, with carved panels under its tall pair; the record's pavilion is a K08 brick projection from its 0.1 m plinth to the gable, with none of them (K08 lays dress bands only on a stone bay's polyline plan, and its plinth cannot reach the basement's top over a storey with lights in it)

the openings' heads (T-3699): the parlour's principal light now stands square-headed under a stone lintel with a carved segmental tympanum over it, and the library's tall pair in moulded stone surrounds under one broad tympanum spanning both, as the photograph draws them; both print inside the deep stone band

the cornice's frieze and blocks (T-3699): a pale stone frieze over the second-storey heads and a row of stone blocks under the corona about 1.0 m apart, as the photograph's (x 540-870 px along the front), now stand under the moulded cornice on the front and both flanks
the cornice's dentil band: the photograph's row of dentils under the blocks; K10's moulded stone cornice lays none

the front dormers (T-3702): the small dormer over the hall is now the photograph's stone face under a projecting stone shelf with a slated hood leaning back over it, its light 0.7 m across; the large dormer over the parlour now carries the photograph's stone coping up its rakes, a short engaged pinnacle with its spike at each shoulder and a finial at its apex
the large front dormer's roundel: the photograph's roundel in its gable (y 290-330 px); K01's lower-face dormer has no roundel, so its gable is plain

the 21st Street flank: the photograph's narrow lights, its projecting bay with a balustraded top and the basement lights under sloped stone hoods; the record's lights at the kit's spacing and its one-storey canted bay; and one flank light under a round arch in the principal storey (x 405-440 px of the flank), where the record's are square-headed

the iron fence: the photograph's low scrolled panels on a stone curb between square stone piers with pyramidal caps, turning along 21st Street; the record's K11 scroll band on taller posts along Prairie Avenue only

the great stack (T-3702): the plain brick stack now carries a carved stone head (the K15 Sherman stack's corbel blocks, corbelled courses and projecting cap) and on it a row of three round flue shafts running back from the street, their tops at the photograph's y 185 px (about 19.0 m)

the great stack's flue shafts: the photograph's stand about 1.9 m over the head; the kit's longest shaft is 1.1 m, so the record's head stands about 0.8 m higher than the photograph's under shorter shafts, and the carved gablet on the head's street face is not built
colour: the print is monochrome; the brick's red and the stone's fawn are the kit's

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
